description: The bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks evaluated across various language families in the context of multilingual BERT models, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis lists language families or groups—IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque—arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” spans from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, representing the total number of probing tasks per language group. IE-Slavic leads with approximately 80 tasks, followed by IE-Romance at around 48, and IE-Germanic at about 45. Uralic has roughly 20 tasks, IE-Baltic and IE-other each hover near 17–18, IE-Indic and Semitic are at approximately 10 and 9 respectively, while Turkic and Basque trail with about 5 and 4 tasks. Each bar is color-coded uniquely for visual distinction, with no additional annotations or error bars. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of Indo-European subgroups—particularly Slavic—in the probing task coverage, while non-Indo-European families like Turkic and Basque are significantly underrepresented.
